title: WISE proper motions show that the variable hot excess of unblended extreme-dust field dwarfs moves with the star, not like a background quasar; part of their constant hot excess can be background
abstract: Question: prior campaign work found that the 3-5 um (W1/W2) excess of many centroid-clean extreme-dust field dwarfs varies over 2014-2024, with W1-W2 near 1 mag, and concluded that mature dwarfs make hot dust in events. Background quasars have the same colour and also vary, and they occur in this sample. Static centroid tests do not find a background source closer than about 0.1-1 arcsec. Is the variable excess on the star? Method: a background source does not move. If a fraction f of the W1/W2 light is stationary, the WISE photocentre moves at (1 - f) times the Gaia DR3 proper motion at any separation. We fitted the motion of WISE single-exposure positions (AllWISE 2010-2011 and NEOWISE 2014-2024) relative to Gaia DR3 for 938 extreme 12 um excess dwarfs, 2,774 matched controls and 67 dust dimmers. We compared each star with controls of equal W1 and proper motion, and fitted alpha, the fraction of the colour-predicted excess light that does not move with the star. Results: controls give no offset (-0.001; 95 percent -0.008 to +0.006). Known blends give alpha = 1.19 (0.94-1.53) for offset centroids and 1.02 (0.53-2.04) for GALEX quasar-like stars. The 26 unblended stars with variable hot excess give alpha = 0.01 (-0.15 to 0.04); the background fraction is below 0.19 (95 percent), and below 0.41 for the 12 with field kinematics. Gaia DR3 5628404318169472 (104 mas/yr) has kappa = 0.977 +- 0.021 where a background source predicts 0.51. Seven analysis variants and leave-one-out fits agree. Unblended stars with constant hot excess give alpha = 0.40 (0.08-0.82), so the static centroid test misses some blends. Conclusion: the variable hot dust of mature extreme-dust dwarfs is circumstellar, not a chance background quasar. Limitations: bound companions also move with the star; only W1/W2 light is tested; small groups; empirical astrometric errors. Job sci-1107-hp-astronomy-46f301308905; topic astronomy; machine hp; model Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5); data NEOWISE-R, AllWISE, Gaia DR3 via IRSA.
